citations.title: Prospect Theory: An Analysis of Decision under Risk
citations.relevance: Foundational statement of prospect theory: the value function is defined over gains/losses relative to a reference point and is steeper for losses (loss aversion) — the core primitive underlying reference-dependent housing behavior.
citations.cluster: Behavioral-economics foundations of loss aversion and reference dependence (housing economics)

citations.title: Loss Aversion in Riskless Choice: A Reference-Dependent Model
citations.relevance: Extends loss aversion and reference dependence to riskless choice, formalizing the reference-dependent preference model directly applicable to sellers evaluating a house price relative to their reference (e.g., purchase price).
citations.cluster: Behavioral-economics foundations of loss aversion and reference dependence (housing economics)

citations.title: Advances in Prospect Theory: Cumulative Representation of Uncertainty
citations.relevance: Cumulative prospect theory refining the value function and probability weighting; provides the modern parametric loss-aversion coefficient often cited when calibrating behavioral housing models.
citations.cluster: Behavioral-economics foundations of loss aversion and reference dependence (housing economics)

citations.title: A Model of Reference-Dependent Preferences
citations.relevance: Provides an expectations-based theory of the reference point, endogenizing where the reference comes from — key for modeling how homeowners' price expectations anchor loss-averse selling decisions.
citations.cluster: Behavioral-economics foundations of loss aversion and reference dependence (housing economics)

citations.title: Loss Aversion and Seller Behavior: Evidence from the Housing Market
citations.relevance: The canonical empirical application to housing: sellers facing nominal losses set higher asking prices and hold out longer, directly documenting loss aversion and reference dependence in the housing market.
citations.cluster: Behavioral-economics foundations of loss aversion and reference dependence (housing economics)

citations.title: Are Investors Reluctant to Realize Their Losses?
citations.relevance: Large-scale empirical evidence of the disposition effect — investors realize gains and hold losses — the asset-market analogue of the reference-dependent selling behavior seen among homeowners.
citations.cluster: Behavioral-economics foundations of loss aversion and reference dependence (housing economics)

citations.title: The Disposition to Sell Winners Too Early and Ride Losers Too Long: Theory and Evidence
citations.relevance: Originates the disposition effect and links it to prospect theory and mental accounting, motivating why reference-dependent losses distort the timing of asset (and home) sales.
citations.cluster: Behavioral-economics foundations of loss aversion and reference dependence (housing economics)

citations.title: Thirty Years of Prospect Theory in Economics: A Review and Assessment
citations.relevance: Authoritative modern survey assessing how prospect theory, loss aversion, and reference dependence have been applied across economics and finance — ideal for framing the behavioral foundations section.
citations.cluster: Behavioral-economics foundations of loss aversion and reference dependence (housing economics)

citations.authors: Kahneman, D., Knetsch, J. L. & Thaler, R. H.
citations.title: Experimental Tests of the Endowment Effect and the Coase Theorem
citations.relevance: Experimental demonstration of the endowment effect, a direct manifestation of loss aversion around ownership — relevant to why homeowners over-value and are reluctant to sell below their reference price.
citations.cluster: Behavioral-economics foundations of loss aversion and reference dependence (housing economics)

citations.authors: Andersen, S., Badarinza, C., Liu, L., Marx, J. & Ramadorai, T.
citations.title: Reference Dependence in the Housing Market
citations.relevance: Structural estimation on Danish administrative data; documents a 'hockey stick' in listing prices and bunching at zero nominal gains, estimating losses weigh ~2.5x gains for sellers.
citations.cluster: Loss aversion and reference dependence in housing seller behavior

citations.title: Nominal loss aversion, housing equity constraints, and household mobility: evidence from the United States
citations.relevance: NLSY79 + 149-MSA house price data show nominal loss aversion constrains owner mobility roughly 2.5-3x more than equity constraints, linking seller loss aversion to the lock-in / turnover channel.
citations.cluster: Loss aversion and reference dependence in housing seller behavior

citations.title: Loss aversion, equity constraints and seller behavior in the real estate market
citations.relevance: CORRECTION: published in Regional Science and Urban Economics, NOT Journal of Urban Economics as briefed. San Francisco Bay Area panel; owners with nominal losses and high LTV sell for higher prices, effects larger than prior estimates.
citations.cluster: Loss aversion and reference dependence in housing seller behavior

citations.title: Loss Aversion and Anchoring in Commercial Real Estate Pricing: Empirical Evidence and Price Index Implications
citations.relevance: Extends loss aversion to commercial real estate; loss aversion strongest at the 2007 cycle peak and present even among sophisticated investors, with implications for hedonic price indices.
citations.cluster: Loss aversion and reference dependence in housing seller behavior

citations.authors: Einiö, M., Kaustia, M. & Puttonen, V.
citations.title: Price setting and the reluctance to realize losses in apartment markets
citations.relevance: ~80,000 Helsinki apartment transactions (1987-2003); disproportionate mass of sales exactly at the original purchase price, evidence of loss-realization aversion in sellers.
citations.cluster: Loss aversion and reference dependence in housing seller behavior

citations.title: History Dependence in the Housing Market
citations.relevance: Universe of England & Wales transactions over 20 years; prior purchase price affects sale prices (cognitive frictions) and selling propensities (credit frictions), core reference-dependence evidence.
citations.cluster: Loss aversion and reference dependence in housing seller behavior

citations.title: House Price Momentum and Strategic Complementarity
citations.relevance: Search model with concave demand curves generating strategic complementarity; explains house-price momentum and amplification of frictions, core to price dynamics.
citations.cluster: Housing-market search, liquidity, time-on-market, and price-volume dynamics

citations.title: Hot and Cold Seasons in the Housing Market
citations.relevance: Search-and-matching model with thick-market effects that amplify seasonality in prices and transaction volume; central to price-volume comovement.
citations.cluster: Housing-market search, liquidity, time-on-market, and price-volume dynamics

citations.title: A Theory of Liquidity in Residential Real Estate Markets
citations.relevance: Foundational search-theoretic model of housing liquidity linking hot/cold markets to selling times, prices, and volume; anchors the liquidity/time-on-market literature.
citations.cluster: Housing-market search, liquidity, time-on-market, and price-volume dynamics

citations.authors: Head, Allen, Lloyd-Ellis, Huw & Sun, Hongfei
citations.title: Search, Liquidity, and the Dynamics of House Prices and Construction
citations.relevance: Dynamic search model of prices, sales, construction, and migration across US cities; key reference for search-based housing price and liquidity dynamics.
citations.cluster: Housing-market search, liquidity, time-on-market, and price-volume dynamics

citations.title: Prices and Trading Volume in the Housing Market: A Model with Down-Payment Effects
citations.relevance: Seminal down-payment-constraint model generating positive price-volume correlation and price-time-to-sale links; foundational for price-volume dynamics.
citations.cluster: Housing-market search, liquidity, time-on-market, and price-volume dynamics

citations.title: House Prices, Sales, and Time on the Market: A Search-Theoretic Framework
citations.relevance: Search model reproducing cyclical comovement of prices with sales (positive) and time-on-market (negative); directly on time-on-market and price-volume dynamics.
citations.cluster: Housing-market search, liquidity, time-on-market, and price-volume dynamics

citations.title: The Microstructure of Housing Markets: Search, Bargaining, and Brokerage
citations.journal: Handbook of Regional and Urban Economics, Vol. 5, ch. 13, pp. 813-886, G. Duranton, J.V. Henderson & W.C. Strange (eds.), Elsevier
citations.relevance: Authoritative survey of housing microstructure: search, matching, bargaining, brokerage, and liquidity measures (time-on-market); ideal framing citation.
citations.cluster: Housing-market search, liquidity, time-on-market, and price-volume dynamics

citations.authors: Fang, H., Gu, Q., Xiong, W. & Zhou, L.-A.
citations.title: Demystifying the Chinese Housing Boom
citations.journal: NBER Macroeconomics Annual (University of Chicago Press)
citations.relevance: Foundational construction of repeat-sales house price indices for 120 Chinese cities (2003-2013); the canonical account of the boom that later reversed.
citations.cluster: China housing market and its 2021-2025 downturn

citations.authors: Glaeser, E., Huang, W., Ma, Y. & Shleifer, A.
citations.title: A Real Estate Boom with Chinese Characteristics
citations.relevance: Diagnoses oversupply, vacancy and price-to-cost gaps, warning that prices depend on curtailing new supply - directly framing the 2021+ downturn.
citations.cluster: China housing market and its 2021-2025 downturn

citations.authors: Wu, J., Gyourko, J. & Deng, Y.
citations.title: Evaluating the Risk of Chinese Housing Markets: What We Know and What We Need to Know
citations.relevance: Documents land values, construction costs and price risk across ~35 cities; the risk framework that anticipated developer and price stress.
citations.cluster: China housing market and its 2021-2025 downturn

citations.title: Peak China Housing
citations.relevance: Estimates real estate at ~29% of GDP and argues an adjustment was inevitable; a downturn could trim 5-10% from output - the macro-magnitude case.
citations.cluster: China housing market and its 2021-2025 downturn

citations.title: A Tale of Tier 3 Cities
citations.journal: NBER Working Paper No. 30519 (published in Journal of International Economics, 2024)
citations.relevance: The tier-3-cities thesis: supply-demand imbalance is deepest in smaller/lower-income cities that hold 60%+ of GDP and housing stock - the epicenter of the downturn.
citations.cluster: China housing market and its 2021-2025 downturn

citations.title: China's Real Estate Market
citations.journal: The Handbook of China's Financial System (Princeton Univ. Press); NBER Working Paper No. 25297
citations.relevance: Survey of the boom's links to households, local-government finance, developers and the financial system - the transmission channels of the bust.
citations.cluster: China housing market and its 2021-2025 downturn

citations.title: The Great Housing Boom of China
citations.relevance: Models China's housing boom as a rational bubble tied to economic transition, implying an eventual correction - theoretical grounding for the downturn.
citations.cluster: China housing market and its 2021-2025 downturn

citations.title: Bunching
citations.relevance: Canonical methods survey of the bunching approach (kinks and notches); anchors the paper's empirical bunching identification strategy.
citations.cluster: housing-paper: empirical bunching methods + house-price-index construction + housing wealth-effect / macro consequences

citations.title: Do Taxpayers Bunch at Kink Points?
citations.relevance: Foundational bunching-estimator paper; the source of the bunching-at-kinks elasticity method the paper applies to housing thresholds.
citations.cluster: housing-paper: empirical bunching methods + house-price-index construction + housing wealth-effect / macro consequences

citations.authors: Wang, X., Li, K. & Wu, J.
citations.title: House price index based on online listing information: The case of China
citations.relevance: Directly supports the paper's hedonic / online-listing house price index construction for China, including handling of replicated or manipulated listing data.
citations.cluster: housing-paper: empirical bunching methods + house-price-index construction + housing wealth-effect / macro consequences

citations.authors: Mian, A., Rao, K. & Sufi, A.
citations.title: Household Balance Sheets, Consumption, and the Economic Slump
citations.relevance: Key empirical estimate of the housing-wealth MPC / consumption elasticity to housing net worth; grounds the macro wealth-effect consequences.
citations.cluster: housing-paper: empirical bunching methods + house-price-index construction + housing wealth-effect / macro consequences

citations.authors: Campbell, J. Y. & Cocco, J. F.
citations.title: How do house prices affect consumption? Evidence from micro data
citations.relevance: Micro-data evidence on heterogeneous house-price consumption responses (largest for older homeowners); supports the wealth-effect channel.
citations.cluster: housing-paper: empirical bunching methods + house-price-index construction + housing wealth-effect / macro consequences

citations.authors: Berger, D., Guerrieri, V., Lorenzoni, G. & Vavra, J.
citations.title: House Prices and Consumer Spending
citations.relevance: Structural framework reconciling large consumption responses to house prices with theory; provides the sufficient-statistic MPC-out-of-housing result.
citations.cluster: housing-paper: empirical bunching methods + house-price-index construction + housing wealth-effect / macro consequences

citations.authors: Kaplan, G., Mitman, K. & Violante, G. L.
citations.title: The Housing Boom and Bust: Model Meets Evidence
citations.relevance: Quantitative housing boom-bust model linking house-price swings to non-durable spending via household balance sheets; supports the macro consequences.
citations.cluster: housing-paper: empirical bunching methods + house-price-index construction + housing wealth-effect / macro consequences

facts.claim: Genesove & Mayer estimate sellers facing nominal losses set asking prices higher by this share of the loss
facts.value: 25-35% (asking); 3-18% realized in sale price
facts.cluster: Loss aversion and reference dependence in housing seller behavior

facts.claim: Andersen et al. estimated loss-to-gain utility weighting for housing sellers
facts.value: losses weigh ~2.5x gains
facts.cluster: Loss aversion and reference dependence in housing seller behavior

facts.claim: Anenberg (2011) journal was mis-briefed as Journal of Urban Economics
facts.value: Actually Regional Science and Urban Economics, 41(1), 67-76
facts.cluster: Loss aversion and reference dependence in housing seller behavior

facts.claim: New-home (newly built commercial building) sales value in China fell sharply in 2024, the fourth straight down year of the downturn
facts.value: 9,675.0 billion yuan in 2024, down 17.1% YoY (residential sales value down 17.6%)
facts.source: National Bureau of Statistics of China (NBS), 'Investment in Real Estate Development in 2024', released Jan 2025, stats.gov.cn
facts.cluster: China housing market and its 2021-2025 downturn

facts.claim: Floor space of commercial buildings sold nationwide contracted again in 2024
facts.value: 973.85 million sqm sold in 2024, down 12.9% YoY; residential floor space sold down 14.1%
facts.source: National Bureau of Statistics of China (NBS), 'Investment in Real Estate Development in 2024', stats.gov.cn
facts.cluster: China housing market and its 2021-2025 downturn

facts.claim: Real estate development investment declined for consecutive years during the downturn
facts.value: 10,028.0 billion yuan in 2024, down 10.6% YoY (residential -10.5%); 2023 was 11,091.3 billion yuan, down 9.6% YoY
facts.source: National Bureau of Statistics of China (NBS) 2024 and 2023 real estate development investment releases, stats.gov.cn
facts.cluster: China housing market and its 2021-2025 downturn

facts.claim: The scale of the sales collapse relative to the 2021 peak
facts.value: 2024 residential sold area was only about half of the 2021 peak (~1.6 billion sqm) and the lowest since 2009
facts.source: Cushman & Wakefield, China Residential Market Report 2024; corroborated by NBS series
facts.cluster: China housing market and its 2021-2025 downturn

facts.claim: NBS 70-city secondary-market (existing/resale) residential price index shows the peak-to-trough swing of the downturn
facts.value: Index (prior year =100) peaked at 110.9 in March 2021 and bottomed at 90.0 in September 2024 (i.e. roughly -10% YoY at the trough), after top-70-city prices had risen ~60% over 2010-2020
facts.source: NBS 70-city property price index via CEIC Data; historical rise reported by GAM Investments
facts.cluster: China housing market and its 2021-2025 downturn

facts.claim: Evergrande, the most indebted developer, was forced into liquidation
facts.value: Hong Kong High Court ordered China Evergrande to be wound up on 29 January 2024, after it failed to restructure roughly US$300 billion in liabilities
facts.source: NPR, The Diplomat, Reuters (Jan 2024); Judge Linda Chan ruling
facts.cluster: China housing market and its 2021-2025 downturn

facts.claim: Country Garden, formerly China's largest developer by sales, also fell into distress and faced liquidation proceedings
facts.value: Liquidation petition filed in a Hong Kong court in Feb 2024 over an unpaid ~US$205 million loan; total liabilities near US$200 billion and about US$11 billion of offshore bonds in default
facts.cluster: China housing market and its 2021-2025 downturn

facts.claim: The 'trade-in / old-for-new' (以旧换新) housing policy was rolled out widely in 2024 to spur sales
facts.value: More than 50 cities adopted trade-in and eased-purchase measures; a nationwide personal income-tax refund lets a taxpayer who buys a new home within one year of selling their old home in the same city recover tax, in effect 1 Jan 2024 - 31 Dec 2025
facts.source: State Council / english.www.gov.cn policy watch (May 2024); ehangzhou.gov.cn
facts.cluster: China housing market and its 2021-2025 downturn

facts.claim: September 2024 stimulus (lower existing-mortgage rates, lower down-payments) triggered a secondary-market rebound even as new-home sales stayed weak
facts.value: Beijing recorded 20,000+ second-hand home transactions in December 2024, the highest in more than 20 months, as buyers shifted toward resale over new flats
facts.source: Caixin Global; South China Morning Post (2024-2025)
facts.cluster: China housing market and its 2021-2025 downturn

facts.claim: Scale of real estate in the Chinese economy and its regional concentration (framing the downturn's macro risk)
facts.value: Rogoff & Yang estimate real estate and related activities at ~29% of China's GDP; tier-3 cities alone account for more than 60% of both China's GDP and its housing stock
facts.source: Rogoff & Yang, 'Peak China Housing' (NBER WP 27697) and 'A Tale of Tier 3 Cities' (NBER WP 30519)
facts.cluster: China housing market and its 2021-2025 downturn
